status: reviewed recommendations; not applied to ranked catalog
method: Live public workflows in isolated browser sessions, using fictional rosters. Pair metrics independently recomputed from visible assignments. Small cases establish these observations, not general solver optimality.

recommendedCatalogAdditions.name: Visora Random Group Generator
recommendedCatalogAdditions.bestFor: Classroom groups with pair rules, label balance, and recent-round repeat avoidance
recommendedCatalogAdditions.summary: Visora combines pasted names, group count or size, together/apart rules, tag balance, local saved-round history, conflict messages, and full-screen presentation. Live tests verified both pair rules and even tag counts, four rounds of nine people without repeated partners, and a warning when repeats became unavoidable.
recommendedCatalogAdditions.pricing: Free public browser workflow with no account required; reviewed 2026-11-03.
recommendedCatalogAdditions.overallComment: A useful classroom grouping workflow with tested constraints and repeat avoidance. Its export surface is limited to copy and browser printing, and it plans each next round against saved history.

ratingComments.easeOfUse: The roster and split controls are direct; optional rules and explicit Save as a round make the history model understandable.
ratingComments.design: Readable cards and practical full-screen output. An invalid setup can leave a previous assignment available, so the error and result need careful attention.
ratingComments.features: Live-tested pair rules, tag balance, recent-round avoidance, saved rounds, custom group names, and full-screen output. No member moves, numeric score balancing, or joint future-schedule planner was found.
ratingComments.outputs: Copy and print controls plus a working full-screen view. No CSV, Excel, or dedicated image/PDF download appeared; browser print-to-PDF is a workaround.
ratingComments.privacy: The tool says rosters and history stay in the browser. Only same-origin resources were observed in this session; that observation does not establish a full privacy audit.
ratingComments.accountFriction: All tested cases worked without signup or payment.
ratingComments.resultQuality: The positive case satisfied together/apart and label balance. Nine people in three trios completed four rounds with all 36 distinct pairs, then correctly reported nine unavoidable repeats in round five. Contradictory rules were rejected. These small cases do not establish performance on larger or harder instances.

pros: Pair rules and label balance verified together
Recent-round repeat avoidance with saved history
cons: No structured spreadsheet or image export found
No manual editing of generated memberships found
Plans a next round against history rather than a whole future schedule
Previous assignments remain available after an invalid setup
recommendedCatalogAdditions.reviewNote: Reviewed live on 2026-11-03. See the dated market report and raw case evidence. Keep recent-round avoidance distinct from a hard pair-meeting cap or a joint multi-round solver.

recommendedCatalogAdditions.name: Pick & Shuffle No-Repeat Group Generator
recommendedCatalogAdditions.bestFor: Recurring groups with confirmed contact history, visible repeat counts, and portable backups
recommendedCatalogAdditions.summary: Pick & Shuffle maintains confirmed group history, searches a next-round candidate, and exposes repeated-pair counts and a simple lower bound. Live tests verified a repeat-free four-round nine-person rotation, a correctly reported unavoidable fifth round, CSV history export, JSON backup/import, and saved-state reload.
recommendedCatalogAdditions.pricing: Free browser workflow without signup; documented limits of 2–80 participants, 2–20 groups, and 50 confirmed rounds. Reviewed 2026-11-03.
recommendedCatalogAdditions.overallComment: A focused repeat-aware grouping tool with useful diagnostics and tested history exports. It optimizes the next round against fixed history and requires stable roster identities.

ratingComments.easeOfUse: Candidate, confirm, and save are separate actions. This avoids recording unused previews, but users must learn the distinction and save again after adding rounds.
ratingComments.design: Clear candidate/history panels and accessible member lists, with useful repeat explanations. The settings and instructional content make the page long.
ratingComments.features: Confirmed history, past-round entry, explicit local snapshots, JSON backup/import, CSV history, pair-count details, and full-screen mode. No skill balance, pair rules, partial attendance, or manual member editor appeared.
ratingComments.outputs: A downloaded five-round CSV contained 45 member rows, and JSON backup/import and saved-history reload worked. Copy and full-screen controls are available. No dedicated PDF/image export was found.
ratingComments.privacy: Roster/history processing is local according to the tool. A request to app.pageview.app was observed; local storage and exported files still expose names to anyone with access to them.
ratingComments.accountFriction: No account or installation was required.
ratingComments.resultQuality: All 36 pairs appeared exactly once across four three-trio rounds. Round five reported nine repeated pairs and a matching lower bound, independently confirmed from the output. The documented bounded next-round search does not certify global optimality for general schedules.

pros: Repeat metrics and a simple necessary-repeat lower bound
Explicit confirmation keeps rejected previews out of history
CSV history export and verified JSON backup/import
cons: Only the next round is optimized against fixed history
Applying a changed roster clears history
No pair rules, skill balance, or partial attendance
recommendedCatalogAdditions.reviewNote: Reviewed live on 2026-11-03. Final five-round test used UI actions with waits for committed state between Confirm and Generate. Raw rounds and independent pair counts are in the dated evidence. The numeric pair-count list is not a matrix.

recommendedCatalogAdditions.name: Peabody Teach Random Group Maker
recommendedCatalogAdditions.bestFor: Classroom groups with assigned roles, pair preferences, and recent partner avoidance
recommendedCatalogAdditions.summary: Peabody Teach provides equal-size groups, together/apart rules, configurable classroom roles, five-round partner history, print/copy, a class-settings link, full-screen mode, and Paper/Night/Chalk themes. Live tests verified pair handling, assigned roles, a repeat-free four-round nine-person rotation, and warnings when rules or repeat avoidance could not all hold.
recommendedCatalogAdditions.pricing: Free public tool with no signup or payment in the reviewed workflow; site says it has no ads. Reviewed 2026-11-03.
recommendedCatalogAdditions.overallComment: A practical classroom group maker with roles, presentation, and tested recent-repeat avoidance. Pair rules are best-effort with warnings, and outputs lack structured file exports.

ratingComments.easeOfUse: Paste names, choose count or size, optionally add pairs and roles, then generate. The main controls and warnings are easy to read.
ratingComments.design: Readable group cards, a classroom-oriented layout, keyboard shortcuts, and distinct Paper/Night/Chalk profiles. Full-screen controls are available.
ratingComments.features: Roles, best-effort pair rules, recent-five-round avoidance, local saved class state, shareable class/settings links, and presentation. No numeric balancing, joint future-schedule planning, or manual membership editor appeared.
ratingComments.outputs: Copy, print, full-screen, and a class/settings link are available. That link does not represent a saved generated result. No CSV, Excel, JSON bundle, or dedicated PDF/image download appeared.
ratingComments.privacy: The site says class data is processed/stored locally and there are no ads. Google Tag Manager/Analytics and DoubleClick-related resources were nevertheless observed. A class-settings link exposes its contents to recipients.
ratingComments.accountFriction: All reviewed cases ran without signup.
ratingComments.resultQuality: Both requested pair rules held in a feasible case and roles were assigned. Four rounds of nine people in trios covered all 36 pairs without repeats; a fifth correctly warned about nine repeats. Contradictory pair rules produced a best-effort result with a warning, rather than a strictly feasible-only result.

pros: Tested pair preferences and recent-repeat avoidance
Local class state and input/settings sharing
cons: Pair rules can be broken with a warning
Only the last five rounds inform repeat avoidance
No structured result export or manual member moves found
Analytics resources load despite local roster processing
recommendedCatalogAdditions.reviewNote: Reviewed live on 2026-11-03. A contradictory Ava/Ben together-and-apart setup produced separate pairs and warned that together could not be met. The initial feasible pair/role case and four-round coverage case passed. Full-screen and theme controls were observed; Chalk was switched on and visually inspected.

How to Make Random Groups
Step by step
Paste your names, one per line. Add tags after a comma if you want to balance groups, like "Ava, girl" or "Sam, 6th grade".
Choose how to split: a number of groups, or a number of people per group.
Add rules if you need them: who must be kept apart, who must stay together, balance by tag, or avoid partners from recent rounds.
Click Make groups. Shuffle again until you like them, then save the round so the next one avoids the same partners.
Show the groups full screen on the projector, print them, or copy them into a message.
Is this random group generator free?

Yes. It's free with no sign-up and no limit on names or groups. Everything runs in your browser, and your class list is never uploaded. See our Privacy Policy.

Document Recompute All Sessions as an online joint-planning action for eligible unlocked golf sessions.
Document current advertised beta limits: 120 members/event, 52 sessions, 30 groups/session, 3 events.
Mention current advertised PDF reports and retain partial export support until organizer access and export availability are tested.
